title: Color Script
body:
Color Script is an ongoing painting practice that explores how color acquires meaning through relationships, sequence, and time.

Each work is created with a limited palette of five colors. The restriction is not a formal rule but a way of allowing every color to remain active. Meaning does not arise from individual colors themselves, but from the relationships they form as the painting develops.

A painting is never planned in advance. It emerges through the act of painting. Forms appear, dissolve, overlap, resist one another, or remain apart. The image is discovered rather than designed.

The works exist at the threshold between abstraction and recognition. They may recall landscapes, horizons, architecture, or places without becoming representations of them. What appears is less an image than a temporary state produced by interacting color fields.

Each painting includes a vertical color code that develops alongside the work. Rather than describing the finished image, it records the chronological order in which colors entered the painting. It is not a legend or a key, but a trace of the painting's own formation.

In Color Script, time is part of color itself. A yellow applied before blue is not the same yellow as one applied after blue. Every color carries the memory of the relationships that preceded it.

Individual paintings are autonomous, yet they belong to a larger, continuous investigation. Together they form an evolving visual language in which every work becomes both a complete event and a fragment of a longer conversation.

Color Script does not illustrate stories, symbols, or predefined ideas. It is an attempt to observe what color does when it is allowed to develop according to its own logic.
Painting becomes a record of these encounters.
